sentences.text: This intra court appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 24.03.2023 passed by the learned Single Judge in dismissing the Special Civil Application No. 5253 of 2023 wherein the petitioner has sought relief for quashing of the notice under Section 68 of the Gujarat Town Planning and Urban Development Act, 1976 read with the Rules made thereunder dated 12.03.1987 with the assertions that the petitioner is entitled for compensation for the shop which is in NEUTRAL CITATION C/LPA/457/2023 ORDER DATED: 06/11/2025 undefined the occupation of the petitioner and forms part of Final Plot No. 243 for an area of 39.20 sq. mtrs.

entities.text: Gujarat Town Planning and Urban Development Act, 1976
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 3. A perusal of the assertion made in the writ petition indicates that as per the claim of the petitioner, the shop in question (area 39.20 sq. mtrs.) was constructed by one Patel Shantilal Mohanlal sometime in the year 1910-1920 and the petitioner's father had taken the said shop on rent in the year 1970-71.
The case of the petitioner is that the petitioner's father continued to occupy the shop in question for the business for which it was taken on rent.
Even the property tax bills and other documents contained the name of the father of the petitioner.

4. It is then submitted that, in the year 1983, the father of the petitioner had purchased the shop in question admeasuring 39.20 sq. mtrs. by way of a registered sale deed dated 19.09.1983 from its original owner.

The said sale deed was registered with the office of the Sub-Registrar and was initially impounded for stamp deficiency, but was released on 27.01.1986 and the registration of the sale deed is incorporated at Sr. No. 1370 of 1986 in the office of the Sub- Registrar.

Entry of the said sale was also affected in the village form no. 6 on 04.09.1986 under the Revenue entry no. 11545 which came to be certified by the Mamlatdar on 29.10.1986.
5.

It is an admitted position on the part of the petitioner that the shop in question was constructed on Revenue Survey No. 567/B/1 paiki which was subjected to Town Planning Scheme No. 30 (Asarwa North Extension) and the said Town NEUTRAL CITATION C/LPA/457/2023 ORDER DATED: 06/11/2025 undefined Planning Scheme initiated under the Bombay Town Planning Act,
1954 came to be sanctioned by the State Government vide Government Resolution dated 24.07.1978.

With the Gujarat Town Planning and Urban Development Act, 1976 (in short as the "Town Planning Act' 1976') enacted with effect from 19.06.1976, the town planning scheme under preparation under the Bombay Town Planning Act came to be finalised with the final sanctioned scheme vide Resolution dated 24.07.1978.
6.

entities.text: Gujarat Town Planning and Urban Development Act, 1976
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: It seems that, in the year 1987, a notice dated 12.03.1987 was issued under Section 68 of the Town Planning Act' 1976 upon the father of the petitioner which contained the information that the original land, viz. Revenue Survey No. 567/B/1 paiki had been allotted Final Plot No. 243.

The said notice was objected by the father of the petitioner and the matter has travelled, at the stage of notice under Section 68, before this Court in the Special Civil Application No. 14175 of 2021.
In the said writ petition, notice under Section 67 to give effect to the preliminary scheme dated 19/23.07.2021 was subjected to challenge.

Upon hearing the learned counsels for the parties, the matter was relegated to the Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation for consideration of the objections of the petitioner and pass a reasoned order after providing due opportunity of hearing.

sentences.text:
After the directions issued by this Court pursuant to the judgment and order dated 23.09.2021,
upon hearing the petitioner, the order dated 18.03.2023 has been passed by the Estate Officer,
which was subjected to challenge in the writ NEUTRAL CITATION C/LPA/457/2023 ORDER DATED: 06/11/2025 undefined petition, out of which the present appeal has arisen.
A perusal of the order dated 18.03.2023 indicates that Revenue Survey No. 567/B/1 paiki was included in Town Planning Scheme No. 30 (Asarwa North Extension) and was given Original Plot No. 150.

entities.text: Town Planning Scheme No. 30 (Asarwa North Extension)
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The Original Plot No. 150 was allotted Final Plot No. 243 after deduction of an area of 392 sq. mtrs. from the total area of original plot, viz. Revenue Survey No. 567/B paiki (Original Plot No. 150).

It is also recorded that on the southern side of Final Plot no. 243, Final Plots nos. 250, 251, 252 were developed by the Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation as slum quarters, on the junction at which the two TP roads of 18.28 mtrs and 9.14 mtrs on two sides were carved out.

The order further records that the notice dated 23.07.2021 under Section 67 of the Town Planning Act was issued at the time of development of the plot in question for construction of 9.14 mtr. TP road and 18.28 mtr.
TP road, carved out from Original Plot No. 150.
9.

It is, thus, finally concluded in the order impugned that in lieu of Revenue Survey No. 567/B/1 paiki, original plot no. 150 in the TP Scheme No. 30 (Asarwa North Extension), Final Plot No. 243,
area 4919 sq. mtrs. was allotted to the original owners after verification of the documents submitted by them before the concerned authority.

As two TP roads of 18.28 mtr. and 9.14 mtr. on two sides of Final Plot No. 243 were carved out, the petitioner being in occupation of the said portion of NEUTRAL CITATION C/LPA/457/2023 ORDER DATED: 06/11/2025 undefined the plot was required to handover the vacant and peaceful possession of the same.
10. We may also note that a notice dated 16/17.09.2021 under Section 68 read with Rule 33 had also been issued to the petitioner as is recorded in the order dated 18.03.2023.

Taking note of the contents of the order dated 18.03.2023 which was subjected to challenge before the learned Single Judge, pertinent is to record that the petitioner is claiming right, title and interest over the shop in question existing on an area of 39.20 sq. mtrs. on the basis of a sale deed executed in the year 1983 in his favour, allegedly from the original owner to whom the Final Plot No. 243 was already allotted with the sanction of the TP Scheme No. 30 (Asarwa North Extension), final notification of which came to be published on 24.07.1978.
As per own case of the petitioner, by the Government Resolution dated 24.07.1978, TP Scheme No. (Asarwa North Extension) came to be finalised on 11.09.1978.

Any subsequent dealing with the land in question after allotment of Final Plot No. 243 to the original owners of Revenue Survey No. 567/B Paiki will not confer any right in favour of the petitioner to seek compensation, independent to that of the original owner.

11. The contention of the learned counsel for the petitioner is that the TP Scheme though finalised in the year 1978, but it has not been given effect to and the notice under Section 67 of the Town Planning Act' 1976 was issued in the year 2021 which itself is evidence of the fact that the preliminary scheme came to be implemented only in the year 2021.

The NEUTRAL CITATION C/LPA/457/2023 ORDER DATED: 06/11/2025 undefined submission, thus, is that the petitioner Hamidkhan S/O Bashirahmedkhan ... vs Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52232863/
3 cannot be denied compensation as he became owner of a portion of Revenue Survey No. 567/B/1 paiki over which the shop in question was constructed.

The submission is that with the purchase of the shop in question of an area of 39.20 sq. mtr. of Revenue Survey No. 567/B/1 paiki, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the scheme of the Town Planning Act' 1976 in view of Section 82 of the said Act.

12. This submission does not appeal to us for the simple reason that it cannot be disputed that the Final Plot No. 243 which was carved out of Original Plot No. 150 from Revenue Survey No. 567/B/1 paiki had already been allotted to the original owner with the sanction of the preliminary town planning scheme, much prior to the purchase made by the petitioner in the year 1983.

Once the final TP Scheme came be sanctioned in the year 1978 itself, any subsequent dealing with the shop in question which otherwise was part of Final Plot No. 243 allotted to the original owner would not confer any independent right in favour of the petitioner to seek compensation under Section 82 of the Town Planning Act' 1976.

13. It appears that it is for this reason, the learned Single Judge has dismissed the writ petition with the finding that on perusal of the documents, it is evident that the preliminary town planning scheme was sanctioned in the year 1978 and thereafter, though the said scheme was varied thrice,
but as far as the Original Plot No. 150, for which Final Plot No. 243 was allotted, the same had never been a matter of variation NEUTRAL CITATION C/LPA/457/2023 ORDER DATED: 06/11/2025 undefined and the scheme, thus, had become final insofar as the Final Plot No.243, which was carved out of Revenue Survey No. 567/B Paiki.

14. Taking note of the above, the learned Single Judge has further recorded that though the petitioner's land was required for widening/construction of the TP road and the scheme was sanctioned in the year 1978, but even after almost 45 years, due to the non-cooperation of the petitioner, the scheme could not be implemented. Sufficient opportunity was provided to the petitioner to challenge the same by relegating the matter in the first round of litigation but nothing could be brought on record.

On the submission of learned counsel for the petitioner about the title or having license of the shop for an area of 39.20 sq. mtrs., it is noted therein that in view the provisions of Section 67 of the Town Planning Act' 1976, all lands required by the appropriate authority in respect of the preliminary town planning scheme, shall vest absolutely in the appropriate authority free from all encumbrances.
15. The assertion that the petitioner was having valid title of the land or having license to run the shop in question would, thus, become absolutely irrelevant and insignificant.

It is also noted by the learned Single Judge that the petitioner had filed the writ petition after preliminary town planning scheme was sanctioned and the scheme had reached upto the stage of implementation.

All arguments made by the petitioner seeking to challenge the notice, the order dated 18.03.2023 and the compensation demanded, are, thus, found to be NEUTRAL CITATION C/LPA/457/2023 ORDER DATED: 06/11/2025 undefined absolutely irrelevant.

16. It is also noted by the learned Single Judge that the petitioner had participated in the adjudication process pursuant to the notice under Section 68 of the Town Planning Act' 1976 once Hamidkhan S/O Bashirahmedkhan ... vs Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52232863/
4

sentences.text: the matter was relegated by this Court in the earlier round of litigation and upon perusal of the order dated 18.03.2023 passed by the competent authority, no error can be found in the said decision.

17. Taking note of the facts from the record of the writ petition and the contents of the order dated 18.03.2023, as noted hereinbefore, we do not find any error in the decision of the learned Single Judge in holding that once the TP scheme had became final in the year 1978, any objection raised by the petitioner subsequent thereto about his right in the land in question, cannot be looked into.

18. We may also take note of the provisions of Sections 44 to 48 of the Town Planning Act' 1976,
which provides for preparation of draft scheme.

A perusal of Section 44 indicates that the particulars such as the area, ownership and tenure of the each original plot; the extent to which it is proposed to alter the boundaries of original plots; an estimate of net cost of the scheme to be borne by the appropriate authority; a full description of all the details of the scheme under sub-section (3)
of Section 40 as may be applicable; the laying out or relaying out of the land either vacant or already built upon; etc. are to be made part of the draft town planning scheme.
Section 40 of the Town Planning Act' 1976 talks of making and contents of a town planning scheme.

Sub-section (3) of NEUTRAL CITATION C/LPA/457/2023 ORDER DATED: 06/11/2025 undefined Section 40 provides that a town planning scheme may make provision for matters such as lay out of new street or roads, construction, diversion, extension, alteration, improvement and closing up of streets and roads and discontinuance of constructions besides other provisions for laying out or relaying out of land, drainage, lighting, water supply etc.

19. At the stage of preparation of the draft town planning scheme in accordance with the provisions of Section 44, the objections of any persons affected by such scheme, made if any, are to be considered by the appropriate authority in accordance with the provisions of Section 47.
Section 48 of the Town Planning Act' 1976 confers power upon the State Government to sanction the draft scheme by publication of the draft scheme in the official gazette.

20. After sanction of town planning scheme, the stage of preliminary and final scheme reached with the appointment of Town planning officer in accordance with the provisions of Section 52 of the Town Planning Act' 1976.

The Town planning officer is empowered to deal with the objections of the persons affected during the course of preparation of preliminary scheme as per the the provisions of Section 52 of the Act' 1976.
Section 65 provides for sanction of the preliminary scheme or the final scheme by the State Government, as the case may be.

Section 67 reads as under :-
"67. Effect of preliminary scheme.- On the day on which the preliminary scheme comes into force - (a) all lands required by the appropriate authority NEUTRAL CITATION C/LPA/457/2023 ORDER DATED: 06/11/2025 undefined shall, unless it is otherwise determined in such scheme, vest absolutely in the appropriate authority free from all encumbrances.

5 (b) all rights in the original plots which have been re- constituted into final plots shall determined and the final plots shall become subject to the rights settled by the Town Planning Officer."

21. A perusal of Section 67 of the Act' 1976 indicates that on the day on which the preliminary scheme came into force, all lands required by the appropriate government, unless it is otherwise determined in such scheme, shall vest absolutely in the appropriate government free from all encumbrances.

Clause (b) of Section 67 further provides that all rights in the original plot which have been reconstituted into final plots shall be determined and the final plots shall be subject to the rights settled by the Town Planning Officer.

22. With the sanction of the final town planning scheme in the year 1978, it is evident that all rights in the original plots which have been reconstituted in the final plots have already been dealt with by the Town Planning Officer.
It is not brought on record of the writ petition that the petitioner had raised any objection during the course of preparation or sanction of the preliminary town planning scheme.

The challenge, for the first time, was raised by the petitioner in the year 2021 by filing the writ petition assailing lthe notice dated 19.07.2021 under section 67 for implementation of the preliminary scheme.
The notice under Section 68 for summary eviction of the petitioner was issued thereafter on 17.09.2021.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/LPA/457/2023 ORDER DATED: 06/11/2025 undefined 23.

From the above, it is evident that much after the settlement of the land in question, viz. Revenue Survey No. 567/B/1 paiki, original plot no. 150, with the allotment of final plot no. 243 to the original owners of the aforesaid plots, the dispute raised by the petitioner in the year 2021 for non- payment of compensation under Section 82 in lieu of the shop in question, area 39.20 sq. mtrs.,
could not have been looked into.
24.

All contentions raised by the learned counsel for the petitioner based on the notice dated 19.07.2021 have rightly been dealt with by the learned Single Judge in the second round of litigation (writ petition) instituted by the petitioner, out of which the present appeal has arisen.
Moreover, no error of law can be found in the order dated 18.03.2023 passed by the appropriate authority for rejection of the claim of the petitioner for grant of compensation.

25. It may also be pertinent to note that in two rounds of litigation, the petitioner has not disclosed as to whom the Final Plot No. 243 was allotted nor the allottee of the Final Plot No. 243 or the original owner, has been impleaded in any of the two writ petitions.

26. Reliance placed upon the decisions of the Apex Court in Shiv Singh v. State of H.P. [(2018) 16 SCC 270] and New Okhla Industrial Development Authority v. Ltd. Col. J.B. Kuchhal [(2020) 18 SCC 619] which are pertaining to the compensation determined under the Land Acquisition Act,
